questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle is projected from the origin with initial velocity $v_0$ at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. A constant horizontal wind force imparts acceleration $a_x = g$ along positive x-axis. What is the equation of the trajectory?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Equations of motion: x(t) = (v₀cosθ)t + ½gt², y(t) = (v₀sinθ)t - ½gt². Note a_x = g, a_y = -g.
Step 2: Isolate t from y: y = (v₀sinθ)t - ½gt².
Step 3: By symmetry (a_x = g down, swapped from standard), substituting t from the y equation into x gives x = y/tanθ + gy²/(2v₀²sin²θ), matching option D.
questions.imagePrompt: A clean physics diagram showing a particle trajectory on an x-y plane with a parabolic path affected by a horizontal wind force vector F_w. Initial velocity vector v_0 at angle theta. White background, exam-style.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A Blackbody sphere of radius R maintained at temperature T radiates power P. If the radius is halved and the temperature is doubled, the new radiated power is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Stefan-Boltzmann Law: P = σ(4πR²)T⁴.
Step 2: New R' = R/2, T' = 2T. P' = σ(4π(R/2)²)(2T)⁴ = σ(4πR²/4)(16T⁴) = 4P.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two infinitely long parallel wires carrying currents I₁ and I₂ in the same direction are separated by 3a. A square loop of side a and resistance R is between them, closest side at distance a from wire 1. The loop moves with constant velocity v parallel to the wires. The induced current in the loop is:
questions.explanation:
Key insight: The loop moves parallel to the wires, so the displacement is along the length of the wires. The flux through the loop does not change with time (the geometry of the loop relative to both wires remains fixed).
By Faraday's Law: EMF = -dΦ/dt = 0. Hence induced current = Zero.
questions.imagePrompt: A circuit diagram showing two long parallel wires carrying currents I1 and I2. A square loop between them moving with velocity v parallel to the wires.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A completely absorbing screen is illuminated by a beam of intensity I (energy per unit time per unit area normal to the beam) incident at angle θ to the screen's normal. The magnitude of the total force per unit area exerted on the screen is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Energy incident per unit screen area per unit time = I cosθ (projected area).
Step 2: Momentum of photons incident per unit area per unit time = I cosθ/c.
Step 3: For a completely absorbing surface, all momentum is transferred. Total force per unit area = I cosθ/c.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a Young's Double Slit Experiment, path difference at a point is λ/6. If maximum intensity is I₀, the intensity at this point is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Phase difference Δφ = (2π/λ)(λ/6) = π/3.
Step 2: I = I₀ cos²(Δφ/2) = I₀ cos²(π/6) = I₀ × (√3/2)² = 0.75 I₀.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls without slipping down a rough inclined plane of inclination θ. The minimum coefficient of static friction μ_s required to prevent slipping is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: For solid cylinder I = ½MR². Equations: Mgsinθ - f = Ma; fR = Iα; a = αR → f = ½Ma.
Step 2: Solving: a = (2/3)gsinθ, f = (1/3)Mgsinθ.
Step 3: For no slipping: f ≤ μ_s N = μ_s Mgcosθ → μ_s ≥ (1/3)tanθ.
questions.imagePrompt: A solid cylinder rolling down a rough inclined plane without slipping. Forces of gravity, normal, and friction labeled.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An ideal monoatomic gas undergoes cyclic process ABCA: A(V₀,P₀), B(3V₀,P₀), C(V₀,3P₀). AB is isobaric, CA is isochoric, BC is a straight line. Work done by gas in the cycle is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Work done equals area of enclosed triangle on P-V diagram. Base = 3V₀ - V₀ = 2V₀; Height = 3P₀ - P₀ = 2P₀. Area = ½ × 2V₀ × 2P₀ = 2P₀V₀.
Step 2: The cycle goes counterclockwise (A→B expands, B→C compresses, C→A isochoric), so net work = −2P₀V₀.
questions.imagePrompt: A P-V indicator diagram showing a cyclic process ABCA for an ideal gas, with points A(V0,P0), B(3V0,P0), C(V0,3P0).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A mass m attached to a spring of spring constant k executes SHM. If the mass is increased by a factor of 4, the new period of oscillation will be:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: T = 2π√(m/k).
Step 2: T' = 2π√(4m/k) = 2 × 2π√(m/k) = 2T. Period is doubled.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An ideal battery of EMF 10 V is connected in series with a 5 Ω resistor and a rheostat. The maximum power deliverable to the rheostat is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Maximum power transfer: set R_load = R_series = 5 Ω.
Step 2: I = 10/(5+5) = 1 A. P_max = I²R_load = 1² × 5 = 5 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The work function of a metal is 4.0 eV. Using hc = 1240 eV·nm, the longest wavelength of light that can cause photoelectric emission is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: At threshold: W = hc/λ_th.
Step 2: λ_th = 1240/4.0 = 310 nm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: **[Passage Q1 — Semiconductors]:** In a p-n junction diode, which statement about the built-in potential barrier is correct?
options: It accelerates majority carriers across the junction.
It opposes the flow of minority carriers.
It acts as a barrier to the diffusion of majority carriers.
It is created solely by forward bias.
questions.explanation: Fact: The built-in electric field (pointing n→p) opposes the diffusion of majority carriers (holes from p to n; electrons from n to p), preventing them from crossing freely. It assists minority carriers (drift). Option C is correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: **[Passage Q2 — Semiconductors]:** When reverse bias is applied to a p-n junction, what happens to the depletion width and junction capacitance?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Reverse bias increases the potential across the junction, pulling more ions into the depletion layer → width increases.
Step 2: Junction capacitance C ∝ 1/width. Wider depletion region → smaller capacitance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which magnetic property is strictly dependent on temperature according to Curie's Law?
questions.explanation: Fact: Curie's Law: χ = C/T applies to paramagnetic materials. Diamagnetism is essentially temperature-independent. Hence paramagnetic susceptibility depends on temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A sound source of frequency f₀ moves with velocity v/2 directly away from a stationary observer and towards a stationary wall. The beat frequency heard by the observer (combining direct and reflected sound) is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Source moves away from observer at v_s = v/2. Direct frequency: f_direct = f₀·v/(v+v/2) = f₀·v/(3v/2) = 2f₀/3.
Step 2: Wall acts as observer: f_wall = f₀·v/(v-v/2) = 2f₀. Wall re-emits 2f₀ towards stationary observer: f_reflected = 2f₀.
Step 3: Beat = f_reflected - f_direct = 2f₀ - 2f₀/3 = 4f₀/3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two soap bubbles of radii R₁ and R₂ (R₁ < R₂) coalesce to form a double bubble with a common interface. The radius of curvature of the common interface is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Pressure difference: ΔP = 4T(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = 4T/R_common.
Step 2: R_common = R₁R₂/(R₂-R₁).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The orbital with n=3, l=2, m_l=-2 (i.e., a 3d orbital):
questions.explanation: Fact: Angular nodes = l = 2. Radial nodes = n - l - 1 = 3 - 2 - 1 = 0. The 3d orbital (l=2) has two angular nodes and zero radial nodes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to MO Theory, which species has the highest bond order AND is diamagnetic?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: CO is isoelectronic with N₂ (14 electrons). Bond order = (8-2)/2 = 3. All electrons paired → diamagnetic.
Step 2: O₂⁺, N₂⁺, and NO all have bond order 2.5 and are paramagnetic.
questions.imagePrompt: Molecular orbital energy level diagram of O2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g), ΔH° = -57.2 kJ/mol and ΔS° = -175.8 J/(K·mol). At what temperature does the reaction become spontaneous?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: At equilibrium ΔG° = 0: T = ΔH°/ΔS° = (-57200)/(-175.8) ≈ 325.4 K.
Step 2: Both ΔH° < 0 and ΔS° < 0, so the reaction is spontaneous (ΔG° < 0) only below 325.4 K.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A buffer contains 0.1 M weak acid HA and 0.05 M NaA. If Ka = 2.0×10⁻⁵ and log 2 = 0.3, the pH of the buffer is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: pKa = -log(2.0×10⁻⁵) = 5 - log 2 = 5 - 0.3 = 4.7.
Step 2: Henderson-Hasselbalch: pH = 4.7 + log(0.05/0.1) = 4.7 + log(0.5) = 4.7 - 0.3 = 4.4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: During the charging of a lead-storage cell, which statement is strictly correct?
options: PbSO₄ is formed at the anode.
The pH of the electrolyte increases.
The concentration of H₂SO₄ in the electrolyte increases.
Pb is deposited at the positive electrode.
questions.explanation: Fact: During charging, the reverse of discharge occurs: 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄. H₂SO₄ is produced, increasing its concentration and decreasing pH.
questions.imagePrompt: Electrolytic cell with a lead storage battery during charging phase.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a first-order reaction A → P, t₁/₂ = 10 min. What fraction of A remains after 33.22 min? (log 2 ≈ 0.301)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: n = t/t½ = 33.22/10 = 3.322 half-lives.
Step 2: Fraction = 2⁻³·³²². log₁₀(fraction) = -3.322 × 0.301 ≈ -1.0. Fraction = 10⁻¹ = 1/10.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ (NH₃ is a strong-field ligand, Co³⁺ is d⁶), the Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Strong field d⁶: low-spin, configuration t₂g⁶ e_g⁰.
Step 2: CFSE = 6×(-0.4Δ₀) = -2.4Δ₀.
Step 3: In free ion d⁶, there is 1 forced pair. In the complex there are 3 pairs. Extra pairing energy = 2P. CFSE = -2.4Δ₀ + 2P.
questions.imagePrompt: Crystal field splitting diagram for an octahedral complex.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which carbocation is the most stable?
questions.explanation: Fact: The tropylium cation (cycloheptatrienyl, C₇H₇⁺) is aromatic — it satisfies Hückel's rule (4n+2 = 6 π electrons, n=1). Aromaticity confers exceptional stability, surpassing resonance stabilization in benzyl/allyl and hyperconjugation in tert-butyl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An alkyne C₆H₁₀ yields strictly ONE product upon ozonolysis followed by hydrolysis. Its structure is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Ozonolysis of alkynes yields two carboxylic acids. One product only ⇒ both fragments are identical ⇒ the alkyne is symmetric about its triple bond.
Step 2: Symmetric C₆ alkyne: CH₃CH₂C≡CCH₂CH₃ = 3-Hexyne. Both fragments give propanoic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: **[Passage Q1 — Organic Mechanisms]:** Reaction of 2-bromo-2-methylbutane with CH₃ONa (sodium methoxide) in methanol predominantly yields:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: CH₃ONa is a strong base. Tertiary substrate + strong base → E2 elimination.
Step 2: By Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted alkene (2-methyl-2-butene, trisubstituted) is the major product.
questions.imagePrompt: Reaction scheme: alkyl halide with KOH/alcohol leading to elimination.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: **[Passage Q2 — Organic Mechanisms]:** 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane treated with CH₃OH (no alkoxide) and gently heated. The major mechanism and product are:
options: Major product is alkene, E1 mechanism.
Major product is ether, SN1 mechanism.
Major product is alkene, E2 mechanism.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: CH₃OH is a weak base/nucleophile. Tertiary substrate forms a stable carbocation readily (SN1).
Step 2: At moderate temperature, SN1 (substitution) dominates over E1 (elimination). Major product: 2-methoxy-2-methylbutane (ether) via SN1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which compound will give a positive iodoform test?
questions.explanation: Fact: The iodoform test is positive for methyl ketones (CH₃CO−) and secondary alcohols with an adjacent methyl (CH₃CH(OH)−). Isopropyl alcohol (CH₃CHOH-CH₃) is oxidized in situ to acetone, giving a positive test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which amino acid contains a secondary amino group?
questions.explanation: Fact: Proline has its α-amino nitrogen incorporated into a five-membered pyrrolidine ring, making it a secondary amine (imino acid). All other standard amino acids have primary amino groups.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A plot of [A] vs time t yields a straight line with a negative slope. The order of the reaction is:
questions.explanation: Fact: Zero order: [A] = [A]₀ - kt (linear in t with negative slope). First order: ln[A] vs t is linear. Second order: 1/[A] vs t is linear.
questions.imagePrompt: A graph plotting concentration vs time with a straight line of negative slope.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A metal salt on heating with K₂Cr₂O₇ and conc. H₂SO₄ gives deep red vapors that, when passed into NaOH, form a yellow solution which then gives a yellow precipitate with lead acetate. The anion in the salt is:
questions.explanation: Fact: This is the Chromyl Chloride Test. Cl⁻ + K₂Cr₂O₇ + H₂SO₄ → CrO₂Cl₂ (deep red vapors). CrO₂Cl₂ + NaOH → Na₂CrO₄ (yellow). Na₂CrO₄ + Pb(CH₃COO)₂ → PbCrO₄↓ (yellow precipitate). Specific to Cl⁻.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The value of ∫₋π/₂^π/₂ [cosx/(1+eˣ)] dx is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Let I = ∫₋π/₂^π/₂ cosx/(1+eˣ) dx. Apply f(a+b-x) property: I = ∫ cosx·eˣ/(1+eˣ) dx.
Step 2: Adding: 2I = ∫₋π/₂^π/₂ cosx dx = [sinx]₋π/₂^π/₂ = 2. So I = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If ω is a complex cube root of unity, then (1-ω+ω²)⁵ + (1+ω-ω²)⁵ equals:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Since 1+ω+ω²=0: 1-ω+ω² = -2ω; 1+ω-ω² = -2ω².
Step 2: (-2ω)⁵ + (-2ω²)⁵ = -32ω⁵ - 32ω¹⁰ = -32ω² - 32ω = -32(ω²+ω) = -32(-1) = 32.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If the normal at P(θ) on the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 meets the major axis at G, and the tangent at P meets the major axis at T (C = centre, e = eccentricity), then CG·CT equals:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Normal at P(acosθ, bsinθ): setting y=0 gives G = (ae²cosθ, 0), so CG = ae²cosθ.
Step 2: Tangent: setting y=0 gives T = (a/cosθ, 0), so CT = a/cosθ.
Step 3: CG·CT = ae²cosθ × a/cosθ = a²e².
questions.imagePrompt: An ellipse with normal at P meeting major axis at G, and tangent at P meeting major axis at T.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If A is a 3×3 matrix with |A| = 4, then |2(adj A)| equals:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: |adj A| = |A|^(n-1) = 4² = 16.
Step 2: |2·adj A| = 2³ × |adj A| = 8 × 16 = 128.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: **[Passage Q1 — Probability]:** An urn has 5 red and 5 black balls. A ball is drawn, noted, returned to the urn along with 2 more balls of the same colour. Then a second ball is drawn. P(second ball is red) is:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: **[Passage Q2 — Probability]:** Given the second ball is red (from the passage above), what is P(first ball was also red)?
questions.explanation: By Bayes' Theorem: P(R₁|R₂) = P(R₁)·P(R₂|R₁)/P(R₂) = (1/2)(7/12) / (1/2) = 7/12.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The sum of the series 1 + 2/3 + 6/3² + 10/3³ + 14/3⁴ + ... up to infinity is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Split: 1 + S₁ where S₁ = 2/3 + 6/9 + 10/27 + ... (AGP with a=2, d=4, r=1/3).
Step 2: S₁ using AGP formula: (2/3)S₁ = 2/3 + 4/9 + 4/27 + ... = 2/3 + (4/9)/(2/3) = 4/3. S₁ = 2.
Step 3: Total = 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The general solution of dy/dx + y tanx = secx is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Integrating factor = e^(∫tanx dx) = e^(ln secx) = secx.
Step 2: y·secx = ∫secx·secx dx + c = ∫sec²x dx + c = tanx + c.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The angle between the planes 2x - y + z = 6 and x + y + 2z = 7 is:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The maximum value of 3cosθ + 4sinθ + 5 is:
questions.explanation: Fact: Max of (a cosθ + b sinθ) = √(a²+b²) = √(9+16) = 5. Maximum of the full expression = 5 + 5 = 10.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In a class of 100 students: 50 like Math, 40 like Physics, 45 like Chemistry. 20 like Math & Physics, 15 like Physics & Chemistry, 25 like Math & Chemistry, 10 like all three. How many like none?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: By inclusion-exclusion: |M∪P∪C| = 50+40+45 - 20-15-25 + 10 = 135 - 60 + 10 = 85.
Step 2: None = 100 - 85 = 15.
questions.imagePrompt: A Venn diagram with three intersecting sets M, P, C with labeled values.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The value of lim(x→0) [(tanx - sinx)/x³] is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: (tanx - sinx)/x³ = sinx(1-cosx)/(x³·cosx).
Step 2: = (sinx/x)·(1-cosx/x²)·(1/cosx) → 1 × 1/2 × 1 = 1/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The coefficient of x⁷ in the expansion of (1 - x - x² + x³)⁶ is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: 1 - x - x² + x³ = (1-x)²(1+x). So expression = (1-x)¹²(1+x)⁶.
Step 2: Need coefficient of x⁷: Σ C(12,r)(-1)ʳ·C(6,k) with r+k=7. Summing all valid (r,k) pairs gives -144.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The statement (p⇒q) ∧ (q⇒~p) is logically equivalent to:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: (p⇒q) ≡ (~p∨q); (q⇒~p) ≡ (~q∨~p).
Step 2: AND: (~p∨q)∧(~p∨~q) = ~p∨(q∧~q) = ~p∨F = ~p.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The coordinates of the point on the parabola y² = 8x which is at minimum distance from the circle x² + (y+6)² = 1 are:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Minimum distance from parabola to circle occurs along the normal to the parabola passing through the circle's center (0,-6).
Step 2: Normal in parametric form: y = -tx + 4t + 2t³ (for y²=8x, a=2). Passing through (0,-6): 2t³+4t+6=0 → t³+2t+3=0 → t=-1.
Step 3: Point = (at², 2at) = (2,-4).
questions.imagePrompt: Parabola y²=8x with a point P and the circle center (0,-6) shown.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Based on a pedigree showing two normal parents with an affected daughter, the most likely mode of inheritance is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Both parents are unaffected but have an affected daughter → rules out dominant inheritance (at least one parent would be affected).
Step 2: An affected daughter with an unaffected father rules out X-linked recessive (father would need to be affected).
Step 3: Therefore: Autosomal Recessive (both parents are carriers, Aa × Aa → aa daughter).
questions.imagePrompt: A pedigree chart showing autosomal recessive trait with carrier parents.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A mutant cell lacks G1/S cyclins. The most likely consequence is:
options: Rb protein remains unphosphorylated, halting DNA replication.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: G1/S cyclins (e.g., Cyclin E) phosphorylate the Rb (Retinoblastoma) protein.
Step 2: Unphosphorylated Rb sequesters E2F transcription factors, preventing expression of S-phase genes.
Step 3: Without cyclins, Rb stays unphosphorylated → cells arrest in G1 (not S phase).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: At a chemical synapse, the influx of which ion into the presynaptic terminal directly triggers exocytosis of neurotransmitter vesicles?
questions.explanation: Fact: An action potential at the terminal opens voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels. Ca²⁺ entering the terminal triggers fusion of synaptic vesicles with the presynaptic membrane (exocytosis) and release of neurotransmitters.
questions.imagePrompt: Diagram of a synapse showing vesicles, synaptic cleft, and Ca²⁺ influx.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the C₄ pathway of photosynthesis, the primary CO₂ acceptor in mesophyll cells is:
questions.explanation: Fact: In C₄ mesophyll cells, PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ onto PEP (3-carbon compound) to form Oxaloacetate (OAA — the first 4-carbon product). PEP is the acceptor; OAA is the product.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: **[Passage Q1 — lac operon]:** A mutant E. coli has a non-functional repressor (i⁻). When lactose is ABSENT and glucose is PRESENT, expression of the lac operon will be:
options: Only the z gene is expressed
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Non-functional repressor → operon cannot be repressed (constitutive derepression).
Step 2: But maximum expression also requires CAP-cAMP (positive control). Glucose present → low cAMP → CAP inactive → poor RNA polymerase binding.
Step 3: Result: basal (low) level expression only.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: **[Passage Q2 — lac operon]:** An operator-constitutive mutation (oᶜ) combined with wild-type i⁺ gene. When lactose is absent, the lac operon will:
options: Have repressor bind permanently to the operator.
Be transcribed constitutively, as repressor cannot bind the mutated operator.
questions.explanation: Fact: The oᶜ mutation alters the operator sequence so the wild-type repressor (from i⁺) can no longer bind it. Without the ability to block RNA polymerase, transcription occurs constitutively regardless of inducer (lactose) presence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis by plants is called:
questions.explanation: Fact: GPP = total rate of photosynthesis (organic matter production). NPP = GPP - Respiration losses. Secondary productivity = rate of new organic matter production by consumers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hormone acts via a secondary messenger (cAMP) because it cannot cross the target cell membrane?
questions.explanation: Fact: Steroid hormones (cortisol, aldosterone, estrogen) are lipid-soluble and bind intracellular receptors. Glucagon (peptide hormone) is water-soluble, binds a cell-surface receptor, and signals via adenylyl cyclase → cAMP (second messenger).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A foreign gene is inserted into the BamHI site of pBR322 (located within the tetR gene). The recombinant E. coli cells will be:
options: Resistant to both Ampicillin and Tetracycline.
Resistant to Tetracycline but sensitive to Ampicillin.
Resistant to Ampicillin but sensitive to Tetracycline.
Sensitive to both Ampicillin and Tetracycline.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Inserting into BamHI (within tetR) disrupts the tetR gene by insertional inactivation → no tetracycline resistance.
Step 2: ampR gene is undisturbed → ampicillin resistance is retained.
questions.imagePrompt: Schematic of pBR322 plasmid with ampR, tetR, BamHI site, and ori labeled.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Casparian strips in the root endodermis are primarily composed of:
questions.explanation: Fact: Casparian strips are waxy, water-impermeable bands on the radial and transverse cell walls of endodermal cells, composed primarily of suberin. They force water and ions through the symplast pathway, allowing selective uptake.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a population of 10,000 with disease frequency 1/10,000 (autosomal recessive, Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium), the number of heterozygous carriers is approximately:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: q² = 1/10,000 → q = 0.01. p = 0.99.
Step 2: 2pq = 2×0.99×0.01 = 0.0198.
Step 3: Carriers = 0.0198 × 10,000 = 198.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The antigen-binding site (paratope) of an antibody molecule is formed by:
options: The constant regions of one heavy and one light chain.
The variable regions of one heavy and one light chain.
The variable region of two heavy chains only.
The constant region of two light chains only.
questions.explanation: Fact: Each antigen-binding site (Fab region) is formed jointly by the highly variable N-terminal regions of one heavy chain (V_H) and one light chain (V_L). The constant regions form the Fc stem which mediates effector functions.
questions.imagePrompt: Schematic of an IgG antibody showing heavy chains, light chains, Fab, Fc, and variable regions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In human females, Meiosis II is not completed until:
questions.explanation: Fact: Primary oocytes arrest in Prophase I (from fetal life). At puberty/ovulation, they complete Meiosis I → secondary oocyte (arrested at Metaphase II). Meiosis II is completed only upon fertilization by a sperm, producing the second polar body and the mature ovum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During which sub-stage of Prophase I are chiasmata first visible, marking sites of crossing over as homologous chromosomes begin to separate?
questions.explanation: Fact: Diplotene: The synaptonemal complex dissolves and homologs repel each other but remain attached at chiasmata (sites of crossing over from pachytene). Chiasmata are first visualized in diplotene.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which combination of characteristics is strictly unique to mammals (found in no other vertebrate class)?
options: Presence of hair and mammary glands.
Lungs for respiration and closed circulatory system.
questions.explanation: Fact: Four-chambered hearts and warm-bloodedness are also present in birds. Viviparity and internal fertilization occur in some fish and reptiles. Lungs and closed circulation are shared by many vertebrates. Hair (or fur) and mammary glands (for milk production) are exclusive defining features of Class Mammalia.
